nodes.summary: For bit lists $x$ and $w$, the canonical bitstring encoding of the pair $(x, w)$ is the concatenation of three parts: every bit $b$ of $x$, in order, written as the six bits true, true, true, $b$, true, false; then a single false; then every bit $b$ of $w$, in order, written as the three bits true, $b$, false.
nodes.title: Canonical encoding of a pair of bit lists

nodes.summary: A polynomial-time computation of the identity map on pairs $(x, w)$ of bit lists, from the canonical bitstring encoding of $(x, w)$ to the verifier's pair encoding of $(x, w)$ (the bits of $x$, the separator, then the bits of $w$), by the converter machine, with the bits and the verifier's symbols themselves as input and output alphabets and time bound $n + 5$: started on the canonical encoding of $(x, w)$, a list…
nodes.title: Polynomial-time conversion to the verifier's pair encoding

nodes.summary: For bit lists $x$ and $w$, the converter program goes in exactly $2|x| + 2|w| + 5$ steps from the configuration at the label *read first*, with no bit in the state, the input stack holding every bit $b$ of $x$ in order as the six bits true, true, true, $b$, true, false, then a single false, then every bit $b$ of $w$ in order as the three bits true, $b$, false, and the other three stacks empty, to the halted…
nodes.title: Full run of the pair-encoding converter

nodes.summary: For a bit list $x$, the bit list obtained by replacing every bit $b$ of $x$, in order, with the six bits true, true, true, $b$, true, false.
nodes.title: Converter encoding of the first component

nodes.summary: For a bit list $w$, the bit list obtained by replacing every bit $b$ of $w$, in order, with the three bits true, $b$, false.
nodes.title: Converter encoding of the second component

nodes.summary: The five labels of the converter program: read the first component, read the second component, emit the second component, emit the separator, and emit the first component.
nodes.title: Labels of the pair-encoding converter

nodes.summary: The program over the converter's four stacks, five labels and states (a bit or nothing). Each pop either stores the popped bit in the state (nothing if the stack is empty) or leaves the state unchanged, and each push of the stored bit uses false when the state holds nothing.
nodes.title: Program of the pair-encoding converter

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and configurations $c$ and $d$ of the converter, the statement that $n$ steps of the converter program lead from $c$ to $d$.
nodes.title: Runs of the pair-encoding converter

nodes.summary: The internal state of the converter is an optional bit: either a bit or nothing. It records the last bit the program stored.
nodes.title: State of the pair-encoding converter

nodes.summary: For bit lists $i$, $a$, $b$ and a list $o$ of verifier symbols, the contents of the converter's four stacks with $i$ on the input stack, $o$ on the output stack, $a$ on the first stash and $b$ on the second stash.
nodes.title: Stack contents of the pair-encoding converter

nodes.summary: The machine that rewrites the canonical encoding of a pair of bit lists into the verifier's input form has four stacks: the input stack, the output stack, and two stash stacks, one for each component of the pair.
nodes.title: Stacks of the pair-encoding converter

nodes.summary: The converter is the finite multi-stack Turing machine whose stacks are the input stack, the output stack and the two stash stacks, with bits as the alphabet of every stack except the output stack, which holds the verifier's symbols. Its labels are the five phases (read the first component, read the second, emit the second, emit the separator, emit the first), and it starts in the phase that reads the first…
nodes.title: The pair-encoding converter machine

nodes.summary: The output stack of the converter has as its alphabet the verifier's work alphabet $G = \{0,1\} \sqcup (\{0,1\} \cup \{\#\})$; the input stack and the two stash stacks have the bits $\{0,1\}$ as their alphabet.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
